result.rationale: The server-side schema (addGuests.schema.ts: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) has no dedupe or case normalization, and addGuests.handler.ts filters existing attendees with exact `guest === attendee.email` while the blacklist lowercases env emails but not the guest strings. `createMany` would then insert duplicate or case-variant attendee rows, and blacklist/existing-attendee checks can be bypassed via case variants. The client-side uniqueness refine does not protect the API boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` but there is no server-side dedupe of duplicates within the `guests` array, so the same email repeated in one request will be passed through and included multiple times in `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows. Additionally, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but `guest` is not normalized (nor are `booking.attendees[].email`), so case variants (e.g., `Test@x.com`) can bypass both `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and the existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email`. The schema (addGuests.schema.ts) also doesn’t enforce uniqueness/case normalization server-side.
